matches.quote: The 0° SQUID is used only as a zero-field diode control. It is not reported to give φ₁₂ ≡ 0 under the identical in-plane sweep protocol.
report φ₁₂, η′(B = 0) and A₂/A₁ versus temperature for several devices... These data are taken at 20 K while all other characterization is at 60–74 K.
The φ₁₂ ≈ π intercept has no absolute flux reference, so extrinsic offsets, coil misalignment and vortex trapping are not excluded... History dependence also points to flux trapping.
The extraction makes several unverified assumptions: ... I_s2 ≫ I_s1 with φ₂ constant, although the areal ratio is only 3:1 and β ~ 1
A clean φ₁₂ ≈ π is inconsistent with the measured, first-harmonic-dominated modulation... they would lie below the |I₂| > I₁/2 threshold needed for TRSB minima to exist
A conventional 0–π SQUID from twist or interface inhomogeneity across the two arms is not ruled out... giving φ₁₂ = π with no chirality
thermally activated premature switching suppresses and broadens I_s, and distorts I_s(Φ) and polarity asymmetries... The authors should present switching-current distributions (widths)
The inhomogeneity-induced TRSB scenario of Yuan et al. is a further alternative... The paper claims to go beyond it but does not test it.
At present the link exists only in SI 10 and the cartoon of Fig. 3(c, d). The authors should move the free-energy/RCSJ analysis into the main text.
The extracted values in Extended Data Fig. 2 scatter widely: roughly 0.7π–0.95π (or 0.8π–π) for "half-integer" and 0.05π–0.25π for "integer".
1/L_J of a tunnel junction tracks I_c(T)... and is not the bulk superfluid density, so comparing it with bulk λ_ab⁻²(T) ∝ T² (Osborn thesis) is not like-for-like.
The 0° device has a much larger Jc, hence a different β and L_J/L_geo ratio. Its lack of a zero-field diode effect is therefore not a matched control.

notes: C11 relies on SI device tables not included in the main text, so the review's critique of the single 0-degree diode control and twist-angle consistency (P17) is marked 'partly'. For C4, the review challenges the invalid comparison of 45-degree c-axis junction 1/L_J(T) to bulk T^2 superfluid stiffness (P22) but asks for a tunneling I_c(T) baseline rather than a 0-degree SQUID measurement, so it is marked 'partly'. For C10, the full review text asks for the temperature dependence of phi_12 (points 4 and 6) and notes why 20 K was used (P2, P25).
